common_mistakes.mistake: Pac jumps into the side of Isp or supports Isp from below instead of landing on Isp’s head.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac is not carried upward; bubble side contact can briefly make Pac STICKY, delaying a jump.
common_mistakes.recovery: On the safe floor, step Pac clear, let Isp settle on LIFT, then reboard for another bubble. Historical focused browser probes report this recovery; the physics and repeatable source attack support it, but the report is older and sampled.

confirmed: The first pass correctly read the explicit Pac-on-Isp FLOAT cue, the upper/lower route split, and both-exit goal.
The screenshot’s CROSS and RECONNECT labels correspond to distinct pads; the FLOAT ride and separate routes are real.
missed_mechanics: Isp must stay on LIFT to start the repeatable bubble attack; Pac must jump onto Isp and dismount during FLOAT onto CROSS.
Pac’s CROSS hold opens Isp’s lower barrier; Isp’s RECONNECT latch opens both the lower crossing and Pac’s upper onward gate. This reciprocal order is mandatory.
Partner support is ordinary physics: Pac standing on Isp is carried when Isp rises; Pac supporting Isp from below is not.
changed_judgments: Reasoning and cooperation rose from 2 to 3 because source reveals multiple dependent handoffs, not just one float ride. Timing changed from unknown to 2 because FLOAT and the boarding/dismount interval impose a finite but repeatable window; historical samples do not establish a guaranteed human window. Hazards changed from unknown to 0 because the route has no hazards and a continuous safe floor. Recovery changed from unknown to 1 because several specific mistakes were recovered without Restart in historical browser probes. Control friction changed from unknown to 0 because the key map is disjoint and the historical ordinary-input run reports are reliable; this does not measure human comfort. Execution remains 2: required jumps and dismounting are visible in source and the sampled route tolerated repeats. Novelty remains 2 because partner-as-passenger is a new combination of earlier FLOAT and split-route lessons. Clarity remains 2 because the screenshot names the ride and pads but not the causal gate sequence.
